Benchmark VISTA against standalone differential-expression backends

Source: R/benchmarking.R
benchmark_vista_equivalence.Rd

Run VISTA and independent DESeq2, edgeR, and limma pipelines with the same filtering, design, contrast definitions, and DEG thresholds, then compare the retained genes, normalized matrices, every numeric column the engine reports, DEG calls, and critical plot inputs.

Usage

benchmark_vista_equivalence(
  counts,
  sample_info,
  column_geneid,
  group_column,
  group_numerator,
  group_denominator,
  methods = c("deseq2", "edger", "limma"),
  min_counts = 10,
  min_replicates = 1,
  log2fc_cutoff = 1,
  pval_cutoff = 0.05,
  p_value_type = "padj",
  covariates = NULL,
  design_formula = NULL,
  tolerance = 1e-08,
  return_plots = FALSE,
  edger_test = c("LRT", "QL")
)

Arguments

counts

Raw counts (matrix/data.frame) with a gene-id column and sample columns.

sample_info

Data frame with sample metadata.

column_geneid

Column name in counts that contains gene identifiers.

group_column

Column in sample_info used to group samples.

group_numerator

Character vector of numerator groups for pairwise comparisons.

group_denominator

Character vector of denominator groups.

methods

Character vector of backends to benchmark. Any subset of c("deseq2", "edger", "limma").

min_counts

Minimum count a gene must reach in a sample to count as detected there; also the minimum row total.

min_replicates

Minimum number of samples, across the whole experiment, in which a gene must reach min_counts.

log2fc_cutoff

Absolute log2 fold-change threshold for DEG calling.

pval_cutoff

P-value (or adjusted p-value) threshold.

p_value_type

Either "padj" or "pvalue".

covariates

Optional character vector of additional sample_info columns.

design_formula

Optional model formula (or formula string) including group_column.

tolerance

Numeric tolerance used for floating-point comparisons.

return_plots

Logical; if TRUE, return paired VISTA/reference plots for MA, volcano, DEG count, and PCA views.

edger_test

The edgeR test, "LRT" (the default until VISTA 1.4.0) or "QL"; see create_vista(). VISTA and the reference both use it.

Value

A list with fields valid, comparison_summary, visual_summary, and methods. comparison_summary has one row per method and comparison recording whether the retained gene set, normalized counts, every numeric column the engine reports (columns_compared), regulation calls and DEG sets agree, with the largest absolute difference for the main columns. A *_within_tolerance field is NA when the engine does not report that column (edgeR reports logCPM, not baseMean). Each element of methods contains the VISTA object, the reference results, structural validation output, self-consistency checks, and optional plot objects.

Details

The reference pipelines are written independently of the code they check. They call only base R, stats and the engines' own functions – never VISTA's internal helpers – and re-implement VISTA's documented contract from scratch:

  • Samples are matched to count columns by a sample_names column, else by non-default rownames, else by the first of sample_name, sample, sample_id, Run, run, Sample and SampleName whose values name count columns (the rule documented for sample_info in create_vista()).

  • Filtering treats missing counts as zero and keeps genes whose total reaches min_counts and that reach min_counts in at least min_replicates samples. For DESeq2, non-integer counts (estimated counts from tximport or RSEM) are then rounded, as DESeq2 requires.

  • Tests are DESeq2's Wald test via results(), edgeR's glmLRT() or, with edger_test = "QL", glmQLFit() and glmQLFTest(), and limma's eBayes() after voom().

  • Design is ~ covariates + group for DESeq2 and the same terms without an intercept for edgeR and limma-voom, or design_formula when supplied.

  • Contrasts for edgeR and limma are the difference between the design rows of two samples that differ only in group, so they do not depend on how design columns are named or which level is the reference.

  • DEG calls are Up when log2FC >= log2fc_cutoff and the selected p-value <= pval_cutoff, Down symmetrically, and Other otherwise, including when the engine reports no p-value.

VISTA's DE tables and normalized counts are read through its exported accessors (comparisons(), norm_counts()). The MA, PCA and DEG-count checks read the data get_ma_plot(), get_pca_plot() and the DEG-count plots draw; the volcano check rebuilds its inputs from the stored table. Rows are matched by gene identifier, not position, and the set of comparisons must agree as well. A defect in sample matching, design construction, contrast signs, DEG calling or row alignment therefore shows up as a mismatch instead of being reproduced on both sides. The two sides share only the engines and the contract above: the benchmark checks that VISTA runs DESeq2, edgeR and limma faithfully, not that those packages are correct.

Examples

v <- example_vista()
si <- as.data.frame(sample_info(v))
data("count_data", package = "VISTA")
count_subset <- count_data[seq_len(500), c("gene_id", si$sample_names), drop = FALSE]

bm <- benchmark_vista_equivalence(
  counts = count_subset,
  sample_info = si,
  column_geneid = "gene_id",
  group_column = "cond_long",
  group_numerator = "treatment1",
  group_denominator = "control",
  methods = "limma",
  min_counts = 5,
  min_replicates = 1
)
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes

bm$comparison_summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 25
#>   method comparison            n_genes gene_sets_identical up_genes_identical
#>   <chr>  <chr>                   <int> <lgl>               <lgl>             
#> 1 limma  treatment1_VS_control     423 TRUE                TRUE              
#> # ℹ 20 more variables: down_genes_identical <lgl>, deg_sets_identical <lgl>,
#> #   regulation_identical <lgl>, norm_counts_identical <lgl>,
#> #   baseMean_within_tolerance <lgl>, log2fc_within_tolerance <lgl>,
#> #   pvalue_within_tolerance <lgl>, padj_within_tolerance <lgl>,
#> #   all_columns_within_tolerance <lgl>, columns_compared <chr>,
#> #   columns_not_in_reference <chr>, max_abs_norm_counts_diff <dbl>,
#> #   max_abs_baseMean_diff <dbl>, max_abs_log2fc_diff <dbl>, …

# \donttest{
data("count_data", package = "VISTA")
data("sample_metadata", package = "VISTA")

target_groups <- c("control", "treatment1")
sample_subset <- sample_metadata[sample_metadata$cond_long %in% target_groups, ]
count_subset <- count_data[seq_len(150), c("gene_id", sample_subset$sample_names)]

bm <- benchmark_vista_equivalence(
  counts = count_subset,
  sample_info = sample_subset,
  column_geneid = "gene_id",
  group_column = "cond_long",
  group_numerator = "treatment1",
  group_denominator = "control",
  methods = c("deseq2", "edger"),
  min_counts = 5,
  min_replicates = 1
)
#> The default `edger_test` in `benchmark_vista_equivalence()` changes from "LRT" to "QL" in VISTA 1.4.0. Set `edger_test = "LRT"` to keep the current results, or `edger_test = "QL"` to use the new default now. The edgeR authors recommend the quasi-likelihood F-test for bulk RNA-seq; the likelihood-ratio test is liberal with few replicates.
